args.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import interp1d

# Load data
data = files[0]['table']
x = data['raman_shift_cm-1']
y = data['intensity']

# Filter for the interval 980-1020 cm-1
mask = (x >= 980) & (x <= 1020)
x_sub = x[mask]
y_sub = y[mask]

# Find peak and baseline
i_max = np.argmax(y_sub)
y_max = y_sub[i_max]
x_max = x_sub[i_max]

# Simple baseline: average of the first and last point in the interval
y_min = (y_sub[0] + y_sub[-1]) / 2

half_height_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) / 2

# Find crossings via interpolation
# We split the data into left of peak and right of peak to find unique crossing points
x_left = x_sub[:i_max+1]
y_left = y_sub[:i_max+1]
x_right = x_sub[i_max:]
y_right = y_sub[i_max:]

# Interpolate to find exact crossing points
f_left = interp1d(y_left, x_left)
f_right = interp1d(y_right, x_right)

try:
    x_low = f_left(half_height_val)
    x_high = f_right(half_height_val)
    fwhm = x_high - x_low
    print(f"Peak position: {x_max:.2f} cm-1")
    print(f"Peak intensity: {y_max:.2f}")
    print(f"Baseline (avg edges): {y_min:.2f}")
    print(f"Half height level: {half_height_val:.2f}")
    print(f"Crossing points: {x_low:.3f}, {x_high:.3f}")
    print(f"FWHM: {fwhm:.3f} cm-1")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Error during interpolation: {e}. Peak might be too narrow or data insufficient.")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(x_sub, y_sub, 'b-', label='Spectrum')
plt.axhline(y=half_height_val, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Half-Max')
plt.axvline(x=x_max, color='g', linestyle=':', label='Peak Max')
plt.xlabel('Raman Shift (cm-1)')
plt.ylabel('Intensity')
plt.title('FWHM Analysis of Peak near 1000 cm-1')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.savefig('fwhm_analysis.png')
